verdict.rationale: React's own docs cover hydration via hydrateRoot, which attaches React to HTML generated by react-dom/server. They also describe streaming HTML that progressively fills in content before any JavaScript loads. However, the evidence never explicitly says hydration happens progressively or selectively, so faster time-to-interactive is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of progressive/selective hydration (e.g., Suspense-boundary hydration ordering), evidence that pages become interactive sooner, independent or hands-on corroboration.
